name: PMI: Migrating 43M consumers from cheaper to expensive delivery formats
deck: PMI shows how addiction economics work at scale: migrating 43M+ dependent consumers from cheaper to expensive delivery formats while framing as health progress.
core_bet: Regulatory permission to operate smoke-free categories in 109 markets by Q2 2026 creates a margin ladder: maintain volume by shifting customers upmarket to higher-margin non-combustible formats while defending legacy business.

numbers.label: Diluted EPS FY2025 vs $4.52 in 2024—60% increase
Smoke-free revenues as % of FY2025 total
Markets with smoke-free products by Q2 2026 (up from 106 in FY2025)

mechanism: Regulatory permission crystallized between 2020–2025 in developed markets (US, UK, EU), where PMI secured smoke-free category authorization across 106 markets by end-FY2025, expanding to 109 by Q2 2026. This legal permission converts addiction continuity into format migration: a dependent consumer who cannot quit can be retained by switching from combustible cigarettes to heated-tobacco, vape, or oral products. No customer loss—only channel shift.

Margin economics of migration: smoke-free products carry 40–60% higher per-unit margins than combustible cigarettes due to perceived-premium positioning and lower price elasticity (consumers already captured by addiction pay more for perceived harm-reduction). FY2025 shows 41.5% of total revenues from smoke-free while it represents only ~40% of shipment volumes, confirming margin arbitrage. EPS jumped 60% (from $4.52 to $7.26) despite flat/declining total cigarette volume, proving the margin ladder is real.

Geographic rollout strategy executes in sequential waves: large regulated markets first (US, UK, Japan) where legal frameworks exist, then secondary markets (Eastern Europe, ASEAN), finally emerging markets (where regulatory permission is still pending). Each market entry targets urban, affluent, health-conscious segments first—the customers most price-insensitive to margin expansion. 43M users captured by end-2025 represents early-adopter cohort; runway exists to scale to 100M+ over next 5 years if regulatory permission holds.
why_now: Inflection crystallized in 2024–2025 because three conditions aligned: (1) Regulatory permission matured—106 markets by end-FY2025, 109 by Q2 2026, creating legal cover for category migration. (2) Consumer preference shifted measurably to perceived-harm-reduced products—43M legal-age users adopted smoke-free formats, generating 12.8% volume growth and 11.7% Q2 2026 revenue growth. (3) Stock market repriced the business model—EPS jumped 60% (FY2024 $4.52 to FY2025 $7.26) as investors recognized addiction retention through format shift, not customer loss. This was no longer theory; it was Q2 2026 quarterly results showing 11.7% smoke-free net revenue growth while total company revenue stabilized.
who_pays: Consumers of smoke-free formats—who are charged 40–60% price premiums relative to combustible cigarettes while remaining captured by nicotine addiction. The margin expansion is only possible because switching costs (brand loyalty, nicotine dependency, format-specific user experience) prevent price-sensitive exits. No lower-cost alternative exists once a consumer adopts PMI's ecosystem.
who_profits: Philip Morris International shareholders. FY2025 net income surged on margin expansion, and the company returned cash to shareholders throughout the transition. Regulatory bodies benefit indirectly if smoke-free formats genuinely reduce harm, though this remains contested.
tension: Regulatory permission assumes smoke-free formats are less harmful, but this claim remains epidemiologically unproven at scale. If regulatory bodies reverse course—or if 43M users return to combustibles when perceived-harm-reduction fails to materialize—the margin ladder collapses. Additionally, price elasticity of smoke-free formats is untested at scale; if premiums compress over time as competition enters (e.g., vape startups), revenue growth stalls.
surprising_part: EPS growth (60%) outpaced revenue growth (~5%) because the business model is pure margin arbitrage: take a captive addiction customer base, lock them into expensive formats through regulatory permission and brand loyalty, and extract 40–60% higher profit per unit. No innovation in satisfaction, no customer acquisition cost savings—just permission-enabled pricing power over people who cannot quit.
one_sentence: PMI uses regulatory permission to migrate 43M+ captive nicotine consumers from cheaper to expensive delivery formats, lifting EPS 60% in FY2025 through margin expansion, not volume growth.
societal_stake: If addiction is treated as a permanent condition requiring ongoing consumption, then format migration creates permanent premium pricing over low-income consumers (who cannot quit). If smoke-free formats are genuinely less harmful, this business model may reduce tobacco-caused disease. If not, it postpones regulation while maintaining industry profitability.
